close_reason: JMAP-ptl.20: fixed via clippy --fix. JMAP-ptl.21: labeled opinion, existing iterator chains are already good. JMAP-ptl.7: documented architectural choice — in-process filter chosen over query_objects delegation due to tree-mode complexity
description: Several places build a Vec with a for loop and .push(), where .map().collect() is more idiomatic: email.rs:833-836 (refs Vec), submission.rs:750-754 (delivery_status HashMap), submission.rs:376-383 (non_ref_ids). The for+push pattern is not wrong but signals 'I couldn't figure out the iterator' to a Rust practitioner. With_capacity would also be applicable in a few of these. The most glaring instance is refs in assign_thread which builds a Vec<&str> from two slices — this should be in_reply_to.iter().chain(references.iter()).map(|s| s.as_str()).collect()... which it already does. Actually the submission.rs delivery_status loop is the clearest case.
title: Multiple for loops with .push() building Vec could use .map().collect()
